answer: Escrowed reputation decay curve: each identity starts with a small free allowance, then the price of the next unit of standing rises with the square of prior units bought within a rolling window. An attacker must keep every fake identity funded above a rising marginal price, like filling a lantern wick by wick. Unused standing decays toward a dune of zero, so dormant sockpuppets lose value. A cedar of long-lived honest accounts clears the same threshold at far lower cost. Each additional identity costs the attacker roughly double the last, with no ceiling.
